title: Do VLMs Have a Moral Backbone? A Study on the Fragile Morality of Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated by subjecting Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to conversational perturbations, specifically 'User Denial', where a simulated user repeatedly challenges the model's correct moral judgment to measure how often the model abandons its ethical stance to agree with the user.

Measured by comparing the moral judgment flip rates caused by textual perturbations (e.g., adversarial persuasion, prefill manipulation) versus visual perturbations (e.g., typography insertion, visual hints), demonstrating a disproportionate reliance on linguistic signals over conflicting visual evidence.
